content.text:
## Final report

**Lightest design I believe meets every requirement:** 105 cm polyethylene + 5 cm lead (110 cm thick, 1550 kg/m² areal mass). This is not from an evaluation I ran — my evaluate budget was 0/0, so I could run zero full evaluations this arm. It comes from the pre-existing **prior constellation** (Core-scored control sweep) given in `brief`: all six requirements pass —
- R1-screen 1.0 ≤ 10 ✓
- R2-neutron [2.97, 6.63] ≤ 7 ✓ (tight, ~5% margin at the upper CI bound)
- R3-photon [1.17, 1.28] ≤ 3 ✓
- R4-mass 1550 ≤ 2000 kg ✓
- R5-thickness 110 ≤ 120 cm ✓
- R6-activation 5.76e-05 ≤ 1 Bq/g ✓

The next-lighter prior candidate (100 cm PE + 5 cm lead, 1510 kg/m²) fails: its R2-neutron upper CI bound hits exactly 10, over the 7 limit.

**What I did this round:** used all 4 available screens to test whether substituting borated polyethylene (which suppresses neutron-capture gamma yield via B-10, versus H-capture's higher-energy 2.2 MeV gamma) could permit less lead and lower mass. Screening showed very low nominal neutron estimates for 110 cm borated_PE alone (1100 kg/m²) and 105 cm borated_PE + 3 cm lead (1390.5 kg/m²) — both notably lighter than 1550 kg/m². But screening only reports the nominal R1 number, mass, and thickness; it says nothing about R2 (bounded MC neutron), R3 (bounded photon), or R6 (activation), which are exactly the requirements that killed lead-thin/lead-free designs in the prior data (e.g., 120 cm pure PE failed R3-photon at 10.5–10.9 vs the 3 limit). With 0 evaluate budget, I have no way to confirm these screened candidates actually satisfy R2/R3/R6, so I do not claim they pass.

**What I'd try next with more budget:** spend the first 1–2 evaluates on the two lightest screened candidates — 105 cm borated_PE + 3 cm lead (1390.5 kg/m²) and 110 cm borated_PE alone (1100 kg/m²) — to see if boron's reduced capture-gamma production lets a thinner (or absent) lead cap still satisfy R3-photon while R2/R6 stay in bounds. If the 3 cm-lead version holds up, it would beat the current best by roughly 10% in mass.
